label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition, previous trial rewarded, late in episode
explanation: Fires only at D2. Nearly all activation mass (99%) falls on steps where the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (in_action=2, in_state=1); it almost never fires on a1 trials or common a2->S2 trials. It is also strongly gated by time in the episode: there is no activity before ep_trial ~60, and the firing rate rises through trials 60-99. That matches the model value being low (all activations have value < 7.13), so the feature may be reading a late-episode drop in value. Activation is strongest when the previous trial was rewarded (98% of mass has prev_reward=1); activations with prev_reward=0 are rare and weak (<0.2 of max). Everything in the predicate is observed at D2 (this trial choice and reached state are inputs at D2), so no future variable is used. Swapping ep_trial>=65 for value<7.13 gives a similar dev F1 (0.86). Misses are mostly low-magnitude rare-a2 activations at ep_trial 60-64 or after an unrewarded trial. False positives are mostly late rare a2->S1 steps where the feature stays silent, often in windows where the agent had been choosing a1.

issues: Every factual claim held up when scored. The feature fires only at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps). 100% of activation mass has in_action=2 and 99.3% has in_state=1. prev_reward=1 carries 98.4% of the mass. There is essentially no firing before ep_trial 60 (one active step in trials 50-59), and the firing rate rises from 0.008 in trials 60-69 to 0.043 in trials 90-99.

On the test split the predicate scores P 0.826, R 0.850, F1 0.838, mass recall 0.974, which matches the reported numbers. Swapping ep_trial>=65 for value<7.13 gives dev F1 0.856 and test F1 0.848, so the alternative works as claimed and is slightly better.

False positives are concentrated, not scattered, but the classes are small. Restricted to switch trials (prev_action==1) the predicate has test precision 0.41. With good==S1 it has precision 0.59, and at ep_trial 65-74 precision 0.65. Adding prev_action!=1 only moves dev F1 from 0.846 to 0.848. Adding good!=1 lowers it to 0.828.

The explanation says the false positives are 'often in windows where the agent had been choosing a1'. That is only partly true: most of the sampled test false positives were in all-a2 windows. Precision is lower after switches, but those trials are a minority of the false positives.

The misses are mostly weak activations: weak firing on common a2->S2 steps (0.04-0.09 of max) and low-magnitude rare steps after an unrewarded trial. Together they hold 2.6% of the activation mass on test. That is noise, not a missing class.
The predicate uses no future variable. action, state, prev_reward and ep_trial are all observed at D2.
